title: Shared shapes of the analysis artefacts — software-analysis capability
description: The definitions every companion schema of this capability refers to (software-analysis DEC-001 point 3): each artefact kind's id, the status an artefact carries, and a line of text. One home for each shape: the kinds' schemas (`actor`, `term`, `use-case`, `journey`, `revalidation-record`) `$ref` them here, and the capability's commands read the id patterns from here, so the stamp that allocates an id and the check that judges one never disagree. Not a schema of any file itself.

slug.description: A word: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and hyphens — the word a stamp takes and the slug part of an actor's or a term's id.

status.description: Whether the artefact is in force. An artefact is withdrawn, never deleted: its file or entry stays, and its id is never used again (DEC-001 point 3).

actor-id.description: An actor's id: `ACT-` and a slug, stable across renames; the key of its entry in the actors' collection file.

term-id.description: A glossary term's id: `TERM-` and a slug, separate from the term's display name, so a rename breaks nothing that cites it; the key of its entry in the glossary.

use-case-id.description: A use case's id: `UC-` and its number within the project, three digits or more, independent of any grouping by area.

journey-id.description: A journey's id: `JRN-` and its number within the project, three digits or more.

artefact-id.description: The id of any analysis artefact.

unanchored-because.description: Why the artefact is deliberately left unanchored — an actor no code or decision embodies, say. An unanchored artefact is reported, never an error; this is the reason onboarding accepts it (DEC-001 point 9).
